jlbind lets an R package call Julia code without starting a Julia session. The
Julia code is compiled ahead of time into a shared library, and R calls it
through native `.External()` calls.

You need [Julia](https://julialang.org/install/) 1.13 or later, and
[devtools](https://devtools.r-lib.org/) for the development workflow below.

We will refer to an R package that uses jlbind as a *client*.

## Set up your package

From your R package's directory, run:

```r
jlbind::use_jlbind()
devtools::document()
```

This adds everything your package needs to talk to Julia, including a Julia
*binding package* in `inst/julia/`. For a package called `mypkg`, its main file
is `inst/julia/src/mypkgBindings.jl`, and it comes with one example function:

```julia
module mypkgBindings

using JLBind

hello(name) = "Hello, " * name * ", from Julia!"

@rcall hello(name::String)::String

end # module mypkgBindings
```

`@rcall` declares a Julia function that R can call, along with its argument and
return types. Every argument and the return value need a type: the types decide
how values are converted between R and Julia (see
[Types](technical-details.qmd#types)).

## Try the example

`use_jlbind()` has already generated the R function for `hello()`, so all that's
left is to compile the Julia code and load your package:

```r
jlbind::build_library()
devtools::load_all()
```

The first build downloads and compiles Julia dependencies, so it may take a few
minutes. Then call it like any R function:

```r
hello("world")
#> [1] "Hello, world, from Julia!"
```

## Add your own function

Adding a function takes three steps.

### 1. Declare it in Julia

Inside the module in the binding package, write the function and declare it with
`@rcall`. Defaults in the declaration become R defaults:

```julia
shift(x, by) = x .+ by

@rcall shift(x::Vector{Float64}, by::Float64 = 1.0)::Vector{Float64}
```

### 2. Generate its R function

```r
jlbind::update_entrypoints()
```

This adds `shift()` to `R/jlbind-wrappers.R`:

```r
shift <- function(x, by = 1.0) .External(.jlbind$.call, .jlbind$shift, x, by)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="What `update_entrypoints()` generates"}
`R/jlbind-wrappers.R`, which you shouldn't edit by hand, also lists the
declarations:

```r
.jlbind_module <- "mypkgBindings"
.jlbind_entries <- c(
  "hello",
  "shift"
)
.jlbind <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
```

When your package loads, `jlbind::bind_client()` looks up each entry in the
compiled library, `shift` as `mypkgBindings_shift`, the function `@rcall`
exports, and puts it into `.jlbind`. Calls go through `.jlbind$.call`, a routine
in jlbind that turns a Julia error into an R error. If the R functions are out
of date with the Julia code, as when you change an `@rcall` without running
`update_entrypoints()`, calling one with the wrong number of arguments gives an
error.
:::

### 3. Restart R and load your package

A library that has loaded can't be replaced, so restart R first.
`devtools::load_all()` then rebuilds the library, since your Julia code changed.
If you forget, `devtools::load_all()` warns that the development library is out
of date and tells you to restart R.

Repeat these steps as you develop. If you only change the body of a Julia
function, you can skip step 2.

## Export your functions

To export or document a generated function, write roxygen comments directly
above its `@rcall`:

```julia
#' Shift a vector
#'
#' @param x A numeric vector.
#' @param by The amount to shift by.
#' @export
@rcall shift(x::Vector{Float64}, by::Float64 = 1.0)::Vector{Float64}
```

`update_entrypoints()` copies them above `shift()` in `R/jlbind-wrappers.R`, so
roxygen2 reads the function's signature from there. To share a help page, use
`#' @rdname` above the `@rcall` and write the page itself in `R/`, on `NULL`.

To add R code around a call, declare the Julia function with a `jl_` prefix,
e.g. `@rcall jl_shift(...)`, and write `shift()` yourself, calling `jl_shift()`.

## Share your package

An R process can load only one compiled Julia library, so jlbind compiles the
Julia code of all installed clients into one library on each user's machine.
Tell your users, for example in your README, to run this after installing your
package:

```r
jlbind::install_library()
```

Your package must also install and pass `R CMD check` without Julia, as on CRAN.
In tests, skip anything that needs the library:

```r
skip_if_not(jlbind::is_bound("mypkg"))
```

In examples, wrap such calls in `if (jlbind::is_bound("mypkg"))`. Then run
`jlbind::use_jlbind_ci()` to check your package both with and without Julia on
GitHub Actions.
